value_chain_position: low-cost-quartile major copper producer, anchor example for the chain
cost_curve_verified: Agree on the conclusion, disagree on the mechanism: the deterministic proxy reads a 62.9% trailing EBITDA margin in the lowest-cost quartile band, and the company confirms it with a June-2026 quarter cash cost of $0.05 per pound of copper after by-product credits (and minus $0.11 in the March quarter), but the cost BEFORE by-product credits has risen from $2.05 per pound in the first quarter of 2025 to $2.29 in the second quarter of 2026, so the near-zero headline is a silver and molybdenum windfall (a $2.24 per pound credit) rather than a mining-cost improvement.
gm_trajectory: Expanding on rising revenue, but entirely price-driven: gross margin 62.0% in the June-2026 quarter ($2,658.5M on $4,289.0M) versus 53.1% a year earlier ($1,619.4M on $3,051.0M), with revenue up 40.6% - while copper volume fell 3.5%, molybdenum 11%, silver 4% and zinc 14%, and total operating costs rose $202M or 14%.
bull_thesis: Southern Copper is the best-run asset in the copper chain, and the bull case is that the market has permanently repriced what a tier-one copper orebody is worth. Three things support it. First, cost position: the June-2026 quarter cash cost of $0.05 per pound of copper after by-product credits is the lowest in the industry, and even stripping the credits out entirely the pre-credit cost of $2.29 per pound leaves a margin above $4 per pound at the current copper price of $6.652 (COMEX spot, at its 52-week high of $6.6885 against a 200-day average of $5.81). That produced record June-quarter results: revenue $4,289M up 40.6% year on year, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of $2,849M at a 66.4% margin, net income $1,670M up 71.6%, earnings per share $2.01 versus $1.19. Second, scarcity: the company holds the largest reserve base among listed copper producers, widely reported at roughly 51.1 million tons of contained copper with a reserve life beyond 35 years against an industry norm nearer 20 to 25 years. New tier-one copper cannot be permitted and built inside a decade, which is precisely why the incentive price for new supply has moved structurally higher. Third, funded organic growth that peers do not have: Tia Maria was 42% complete at 30 June 2026, targets first production in the second half of 2027 at 120,000 tons a year and an estimated cash cost of $1.16 per pound; El Pilar (36,000 tons) was board-approved in the June quarter; Los Chancas, Michiquillay and El Arco follow, taking the company from 917,000 tons guided for 2026 toward a stated 1.06 million tons in 2029 and 1.6 million tons by 2033-2034. All of it is wholly owned, requires no partner and no equity issuance, and is funded from cash flow plus modest debt - the $1.25 billion of ten-year notes issued on 24 June 2026 at 5.35% was oversubscribed 3.2 times. The balance sheet is the strongest in the peer group: net debt of about $1.2 billion against $9.93 billion of trailing EBITDA, or 0.29 times, with $7.33 billion of cash and short-term investments at 30 June 2026, return on invested capital of 26.2% and return on equity of 49.4%. Management is credibly non-promotional: mine plans are built at a long-term copper price of $3.30 per pound (first-quarter 2025 call), roughly half the current price, and the chief financial officer told the fourth-quarter 2025 call flatly that 'We were not forecasting copper prices. That is not our business.' The conditions this case needs are specific and testable: copper must hold near or above $6 per pound rather than reverting toward its 52-week low of $4.355; silver and molybdenum must not give back the extraordinary gains that produced the by-product credit (silver averaged $73.49 an ounce in the June quarter, molybdenum $29.44 per pound); Tia Maria must commission on schedule in the second half of 2027 without the community disruption that stalled it for a decade; and the market must keep paying a premium multiple for reserve life.
bear_thesis: Every headline that makes this company look exceptional right now is a function of four commodity prices sitting at or near multi-year highs at the same moment, and the share price has capitalised that coincidence as if it were permanent. At $195.475 the enterprise is valued at roughly $164 billion, or 16.5 times trailing EBITDA - against 11.5 times for Freeport-McMoRan and 7.4 times for Teck Resources. The operating base underneath that premium is shrinking, not growing: copper production has fallen three years running (973,000 tons in 2024, 956,270 in 2025, 917,000 guided for 2026), Peru was down 12% in the June-2026 quarter on lower ore grades at Toquepala and Cuajone, and management has guided 2027 copper to be 'more or less the same' as 2026. There is no volume relief before Tia Maria in the second half of 2027. Meanwhile the cost of mining a pound of copper before by-product credits has risen 12% in five quarters, from $2.05 to $2.29. The near-zero headline cash cost is therefore a by-product artifact, and by-products are already turning: silver trades at $60.14 an ounce today against the $73.49 average that produced the June-quarter credit - 18% lower, and less than half its 52-week high of $121.30 - so the third-quarter credit shrinks mechanically. The torque is symmetric and large: the deterministic estimate in the input bundle puts a 10% commodity move at about 13.5% of EBITDA, roughly $1.5 billion on the current $11.4 billion annualised run rate, and copper traded at $4.355 within the past twelve months. The capital burden is rising into that: the decade programme has inflated from 'exceeds $15 billion' (first-quarter 2025 call) to 'exceeds $20.5 billion' (second-quarter 2026 call), a 37% increase in eighteen months while the 1.6 million ton target slipped from 'towards 2030' to '2033, 2034'. First-half 2026 capital spending was $865 million, up 56% year on year, against a cash dividend of $1.10 a quarter (about $3.3 billion a year). Free cash flow is squeezed from both ends exactly as the price tailwind fades - and the true trailing free cash flow is $5.08 billion, not the $5.97 billion in the screener bundle, which overstates it by roughly $884 million because the June-quarter capital-expenditure sign is flipped in the source feed. Three further risks are unpriced. The company refuses, repeatedly (first-quarter 2025 and fourth-quarter 2025 calls), to disclose what share of sales goes to the American exchange, so investors cannot size the tariff-driven premium it has been earning - and refined copper, currently exempt from the 50% Section 232 tariff, is scheduled for phase-in from 2027, which cuts the other way for a Peruvian and Mexican producer shipping into the United States. Peru is mid-transition, with President-elect Keiko Fujimori taking office on 28 July 2026 and an unresolved proposal to redistribute up to 40% of the mining canon directly to residents in producing areas, on which management explicitly declined to comment. And the free float is roughly 11% (Grupo Mexico owns about 88.9%), so the passive and quantitative flows visible in recent filings amplify moves in both directions. What confirms the bear case: a third-quarter 2026 report in late October showing the by-product credit falling while volumes stay soft, or the January 2027 guidance call confirming a third consecutive flat-to-down copper year.
sop_bull: Favorable sum-of-the-parts (valuing each metal stream separately, then adding the growth pipeline), assuming the structural-deficit case holds and copper settles near $7.00 per pound with silver near $70 an ounce and molybdenum near $29: Copper stream - 917,000 tons (2,021 million pounds) at $7.00 realised is $14.15 billion of revenue; at a pre-credit cash cost of $2.35 per pound that is $4.75 billion of cost, leaving $9.40 billion of segment earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; at 13 times, $122.2 billion. Molybdenum - $1.78 billion of revenue at roughly 90% flow-through as a by-product is $1.60 billion; at 7 times, $11.2 billion. Silver - 24 million ounces at $70 is $1.68 billion of revenue and $1.51 billion of earnings; at 9 times, $13.6 billion. Zinc - $0.56 billion of revenue at about 50% margin is $0.28 billion; at 6 times, $1.7 billion. Sulphuric acid and other - $0.18 billion of earnings at 5 times, $0.9 billion. Parts subtotal $149.6 billion. Growth overlay: Tia Maria (120,000 tons a year from the second half of 2027 at a $1.16 per pound cash cost, 42% built) net of remaining spend, plus El Pilar (36,000 tons, board-approved), plus option value on Los Chancas, Michiquillay and El Arco - call it $34 billion at these prices, less the roughly $19 billion of the announced $20.5 billion decade programme still to be spent, so a net $15 billion. Enterprise value $164.6 billion, less net debt of $1.2 billion (borrowings of $7.99 billion plus $534 million of capitalised leases, minus $7.33 billion of cash and short-term investments at 30 June 2026), equity $163.4 billion on 834.3 million shares = about $196 per share on the parts alone, rising to roughly $218 per share once the pipeline is credited at a full multiple. Note this lands just below the 52-week high of $221.67 - the bull case is essentially already in the price.
sop_bear: Adverse sum-of-the-parts, assuming the copper cycle turns against the company: copper reverts to $5.00 per pound (still above its 52-week low of $4.355 and well above the $3.30 the company itself uses for mine planning), silver to $45 an ounce, molybdenum to $22 per pound, zinc to $1.35. Copper stream - 2,021 million pounds at $5.00 is $10.11 billion of revenue; the pre-credit cash cost rises to $2.40 per pound on fixed-cost deleverage and the declining Toquepala and Cuajone grades management has already flagged, so $4.85 billion of cost, leaving $5.26 billion of segment earnings; at 9 times (the deficit narrative is broken and the premium multiple goes with it), $47.3 billion. Molybdenum - $1.35 billion of revenue, $1.22 billion of earnings; at 5 times, $6.1 billion. Silver - 24 million ounces at $45 is $1.08 billion of revenue and $0.97 billion of earnings; at 7 times, $6.8 billion. Zinc - $0.49 billion of revenue, $0.24 billion of earnings; at 5 times, $1.2 billion. Other - $0.14 billion at 4 times, $0.6 billion. Parts subtotal $62.0 billion. Growth overlay in an adverse regime: Tia Maria still works at a $1.16 per pound cash cost and is worth roughly $4 billion, but the un-approved, un-permitted remainder of the $20.5 billion programme becomes a claim on cash rather than an asset - net the overlay to zero. Net debt rises rather than falls: at $5.00 copper the business still covers its dividend, but with capital spending running above $2 billion a year and the $1.10 quarterly cash dividend maintained, assume $2.5 billion of net debt. Equity $59.5 billion on about 838 million shares = roughly $71 per share. Applying the same arithmetic at the milder adverse case that I treat as the working downside - copper at $5.00 but the multiple holding at 11 times blended, which is what this stock actually commanded through the 2022-2023 trough given its tiny free float - total earnings of $7.83 billion times 11 is $86.1 billion of enterprise value, less $2.5 billion of net debt, or about $100 per share. The symmetric torque check: a single 10% move down in copper alone removes about 13.5% of earnings, roughly $1.5 billion at the current run rate.
sop_fair_value: About $156 per share (base case), against a live price of $195.475.
sop_breakdown: Base case assumes copper at $5.75 per pound (roughly the 200-day average of $5.81, between spot of $6.652 and the adverse $5.00), silver at $55 an ounce, molybdenum at $25 per pound, zinc at $1.45. Copper stream: 2,021 million pounds at $5.75 is $11.62 billion of revenue less a $2.35 per pound pre-credit cash cost ($4.75 billion), giving $6.87 billion of segment earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. Molybdenum: $1.54 billion of revenue, $1.38 billion of earnings. Silver: 24 million ounces at $55 is $1.32 billion of revenue, $1.19 billion of earnings. Zinc: $0.52 billion of revenue, $0.26 billion of earnings. Sulphuric acid and other: $0.16 billion. Total $9.86 billion, which reconciles closely to the actual trailing twelve-month figure of $9.93 billion. Applied multiple 12.5 times - a premium to Freeport-McMoRan's 11.5 times, justified by a 66% margin against Freeport's, 26.2% return on invested capital against Freeport's 8.8%, leverage of 0.29 times against 0.70 times, and a reserve life beyond 35 years - but a clear discount to the 16.5 times the market is paying today. That is $123.3 billion of enterprise value. Growth overlay: Tia Maria net of remaining spend at base-case prices is about $7 billion and El Pilar about $1.5 billion; the un-approved remainder of the $20.5 billion programme is netted to zero, since its option value roughly offsets its capital drag. Total $131.8 billion, less net debt of $1.2 billion, is $130.6 billion of equity on 834.3 million shares, or about $156.5 per share. Two independent checks agree: the street consensus target is $162.33 (FMP, median $163.00, high $178.00, low $140.00) and MarketBeat reported a consensus of 'Reduce' with a $148.60 target on 30 July 2026, from fifteen firms of which seven rate it sell.
risk_reward: Unfavorable. From $195.475 the base-case fair value of $156 sits 20% BELOW the price - there is no upside to fair value, there is downside to it. The adverse case at $100 is 49% below. The bull case at $218 offers 12%, and it requires copper to hold above $7 per pound indefinitely. The stock has already risen 119% from its 52-week low of $89.29 and sits 12% below its 52-week high of $221.67. There is no structural floor: net debt of $1.2 billion means no net-cash backstop, there are no deal terms, and a 2.3% cash dividend yield is not a floor.
catalyst_status_note: The re-rate that mattered has already happened - the shares rose 119% from a 52-week low of $89.29 to $195.475 on metal prices and the record June-2026 quarter reported on 22 July 2026. The forward events are real but neither binding nor contractual. Tia Maria was 42% complete at 30 June 2026 with commissioning tests targeted for May or June 2027 and production in the second half of 2027 (second-quarter 2026 call), but it is a company-controlled construction schedule at a project that stalled for roughly a decade on community opposition, and this management's project-timing record is the weak spot in an otherwise strong credibility profile: El Pilar took eleven years from its 2015 acquisition to board approval in the June 2026 quarter, the Cuajone expansion has been under review since the third-quarter 2025 call without board approval, and the 1.6 million ton target moved from 'towards 2030' to '2033, 2034'. The second forward event is a third-party regulatory decision: refined copper is currently exempt from the 50% Section 232 tariff but phase-in is scheduled to begin in 2027, per the Congressional Research Service and the 1 June 2026 presidential proclamation effective 8 June 2026. Per this lane's neutrality rule, this status is descriptive only and does not drive the verdict - the verdict rests on the residual value case.
peer_comps_note: Against the assigned chain competitors, Southern Copper is the best business at the worst price. On trailing enterprise value to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation the company trades at 16.5 times, against 11.5 times for Freeport-McMoRan and 7.4 times for Teck Resources. The quality premium is genuine and quantifiable - return on invested capital of 26.2% versus Freeport's 8.8% and Teck's 5.5%; return on equity of 49.4% versus 15.3% and 9.6%; net debt to earnings of 0.29 times versus 0.70 and 0.58 - but a 44% premium to Freeport and a 122% premium to Teck is a lot to pay when all three are earning peak-cycle margins on the same copper price. A separate check from a January 2026 Zacks note put Southern Copper at 8.67 times forward price-to-sales against a non-ferrous mining industry average of 4.48 and Freeport at 3.09. Note that the whole cohort moved together on 4 August 2026 (Southern Copper up 5.1%, Freeport up 6.4%, Teck up 8.3%, Antofagasta up 6.8%, Hudbay up 5.9%), which is the tell that this is a commodity-price move rather than a company-specific re-rating. Applying the peer-median multiple of about 11.5 times to a mid-cycle earnings estimate of $9.86 billion would put the shares near $135; the 12.5 times used in the base case already gives Southern Copper credit for being the best asset in the group.
consensus_delta: The unusual feature of this name is that the sell side and our own sum-of-the-parts already agree, and the share price has simply run past both. Fifteen firms carry a consensus of 'Reduce' with a $148.60 target (MarketBeat, 30 July 2026); the FMP consensus is $162.33 with a high of $178.00, and the five newest individual targets - $166.00 on 23 July, $160.00 from Barclays on 15 July, $172.00 from Wells Fargo on 9 July, $158.00 from Morgan Stanley on 8 July, $160.00 from UBS on 30 June - all sit below the live price of $195.475. Where we disagree with the market is therefore not with the analysts but with the marginal buyer, and the specific mistake is identifiable. The market is capitalising a by-product windfall as if it were a structural mining-cost improvement. The June-2026 quarter cash cost of $0.05 per pound of copper after by-product credits is being read as evidence of an unassailable cost position; in fact the cost of mining a pound of copper before credits ROSE from $2.05 in the first quarter of 2025 to $2.29 in the second quarter of 2026, and the $2.24 per pound credit that closed the gap came from silver averaging $73.49 an ounce (up 118% year on year) and molybdenum averaging $29.44 per pound (up 43%). Silver already trades at $60.14, 18% below that quarterly average, so the credit compresses in the third quarter arithmetically. The second incorrect assumption is that record results signal operating momentum. Every product declined in volume in the June quarter - copper 3.5%, molybdenum 11%, silver 4%, zinc 14% - while costs rose 14%; the entire 41% revenue increase is price. The third is a data error worth correcting for anyone screening on cash flow: the trailing free cash flow figure of $5.97 billion in our own input bundle is overstated by roughly $884 million because the June-quarter capital-expenditure sign is flipped in the source feed. Computed from the filings, operating cash flow of $6,736.9 million less capital spending of $1,655.6 million gives $5.08 billion, a 3.1% free-cash-flow yield rather than 3.7%, of which $3.02 billion of cash dividends already consumed 59%.
valley_of_death: The next three to nine months contain three separate compressions arriving together, and none of them require a recession. First, the by-product credit reverses on prices that have already moved: silver at $60.14 an ounce is 18% below the $73.49 average that generated the June-quarter credit and less than half its 52-week high of $121.30; gold, a fair proxy for the precious complex, is 26% below its high. Silver is roughly 9% of sales at near-100% incremental margin, so an 18% price decline is on the order of $270 million of annualised earnings, and it lands in the third-quarter report due in late October 2026. Second, volumes keep falling with no offset until late 2027: guidance is 917,000 tons of copper for 2026 against 956,270 in 2025 and 973,000 in 2024, Peru fell 12% in the June quarter on lower ore grades at Toquepala and Cuajone, and management told the July 2026 call that 2027 copper will be 'more or less the same' as 2026. Third, the capital and distribution burden steps up into that: first-half 2026 capital spending of $865 million was up 56% year on year against a decade programme now described as exceeding $20.5 billion, the quarterly cash dividend is $1.10 a share (roughly $3.3 billion a year), and the company issued $1.25 billion of ten-year notes at 5.35% on 24 June 2026 to fund Tia Maria - net debt is climbing from a very low base rather than falling. Layered on top are two events with no reliable handicap. Peru's president-elect Keiko Fujimori took office on 28 July 2026 with an unresolved proposal to redistribute up to 40% of the mining canon directly to residents in producing areas, and management explicitly declined to comment on whether that helps or complicates community agreements - at a company whose flagship project was stalled for roughly a decade by community opposition. And refined copper, currently exempt from the 50% Section 232 tariff, is scheduled for phase-in from 2027; the company has twice refused to disclose what share of its sales goes to the American exchange, so neither the premium it has been earning nor the exposure it would carry can be sized. Finally the pure price risk, stated symmetrically: the input bundle's torque estimate puts a 10% commodity move at about 13.5% of earnings, roughly $1.5 billion on the current $11.4 billion annualised run rate. Copper sits at $6.652, its 52-week high; its 52-week low was $4.355. A move back to the 200-day average of $5.81 alone takes roughly 17% off earnings.
positioning_washout: The shareholder register is structurally fragile in a way that cuts both directions. Grupo Mexico owns approximately 88.9%, leaving a free float near 11% of a $163 billion company. That tiny float is what allows the shares to command 16.5 times earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation against Freeport-McMoRan's 11.5 times, because index and passive demand must be met from a thin supply - and it is exactly what would make a reversal violent. The institutional activity visible in recent filings is mechanical rather than conviction-driven: Dimensional Fund Advisors adding 1.3%, Arrowstreet Capital adding 7.0%, the California Public Employees Retirement System adding 21.2% - quantitative and index-tracking money that buys on momentum and sells on the same signal. A distinct and specific risk sits in the income base. The declared June-2026 distribution was '$1.10 per share cash dividend and 0.0120 stock dividend' with a combined stated value of $3.23 per share; only $1.10 of that is cash. The stock portion is a pro-rata hand-out of treasury shares, which costs the company nothing and gives holders nothing they did not already own, but it makes the headline yield look roughly three times the cash actually paid, and yield-screening buyers have been attracted on the larger number. That mechanism has a finite life: management disclosed about 65 million treasury shares remaining after the third-quarter 2025 payment, and at roughly 10 million shares a quarter the reserve runs out in about six quarters - around the end of 2027 - after which the company must either issue new shares or cut the headline payout. Share count has already risen from 792.5 million in the first quarter of 2025 to 829.1 million in the second quarter of 2026, up 4.6%. Insider behaviour offers no support: zero open-market purchases against 24 sales of 17,516 shares, though in an 88.9%-controlled company that signal is weak either way.
forcing_function: Four dated events, in order. The third-quarter 2026 results call, due in late October 2026 (the company closed the July call by promising the next report would cover the third quarter), is the first period in which the silver and molybdenum credit reversal meets still-declining Peruvian volumes in the same set of numbers - the cleanest test of whether the near-zero cash cost survives without the by-product windfall. The January 2027 report is where management has twice said (third-quarter 2025 and second-quarter 2026 calls) it gives fuller multi-year production guidance; with 2027 copper already flagged as 'more or less the same' as 2026, that call is where a third consecutive flat-to-down year gets formally confirmed, along with any change to the 1.06 million ton 2029 figure. Tia Maria commissioning is the genuine operating milestone: 42% complete at 30 June 2026, with equipment tests targeted for May or June 2027 and first production in the second half of 2027 at 120,000 tons a year and a stated cash cost of $1.16 per pound. And the Section 232 determination on refined copper, currently exempt but scheduled to phase in from 2027, is the one event that could move the American price premium the company earns but refuses to quantify. None of these forces a re-rating upward from here; the first two are more likely to force one downward.
moderator_conclusion: This is an excellent company at a price that has moved past what the business is worth through a full cycle, and the discipline of this lane is to separate those two judgements. On the operating merits Southern Copper deserves everything said about it: the lowest cash cost in the industry even before by-product credits ($2.29 per pound against a copper price above $6), the largest reserve base among listed copper producers at roughly 51.1 million tons with a reserve life beyond 35 years, return on invested capital of 26.2%, net debt of $1.2 billion against $9.93 billion of trailing earnings, and a wholly-owned, self-funded growth pipeline that takes production from 917,000 tons toward a stated 1.6 million tons in the mid-2030s. Management is specific, numerate, delivers what it guides (2025 copper missed by 1% with the shortfall flagged in stages; molybdenum, silver and zinc all beat), builds its mine plans at a $3.30 per pound copper price - roughly half spot - and refuses on principle to forecast the copper price. Credibility is high, the moat is wide and stable, and there is no structural force impairing the terminal value of these orebodies; copper is on the winning side of electrification and data-centre build-out. What fails is the price. At $195.475 the enterprise trades at 16.5 times trailing earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, against 11.5 times for Freeport-McMoRan and 7.4 times for Teck Resources, and those trailing earnings are themselves a peak: copper at its 52-week high, silver up 118% year on year, molybdenum up 43%, all at once. Reconciling the favorable and adverse parts valuations on a mid-cycle deck - copper at the 200-day average of $5.75-5.81, silver at $55, molybdenum at $25, valued at 12.5 times, a full turn of premium over Freeport for genuinely superior economics - gives about $156 per share, twenty percent below the market. The favorable case reaches $218 only if copper holds above $7 permanently, and that is twelve percent away. The adverse case, which needs nothing worse than copper reverting to $5.00 while the premium multiple compresses to eleven times, is roughly $100 - a level the shares traded through within the past year. Three specific things make this worse than a simple valuation call. The near-zero headline cash cost is a by-product mirage that is already unwinding: silver at $60.14 today is 18% below the average that produced the June-quarter credit. Volumes have fallen three years running with no relief before the second half of 2027. And the capital burden inflated 37% in eighteen months, from 'exceeds $15 billion' to 'exceeds $20.5 billion', while the 1.6 million ton date slipped from 'towards 2030' to '2033, 2034'. The verdict is to pass for now, and the value case is rated the same way: the business would earn a high mark, the price does not, and there is no discount here to underwrite. This is not a value trap - there is nothing melting - which is why the score is a two rather than a one. The level to watch is the mid-cycle fair value: this becomes interesting in the $130 to $145 range, where the mid-cycle earnings power is available at a peer-appropriate multiple and the reserve life and growth pipeline come free. Given how thin the free float is, that range is reachable on nothing more dramatic than copper returning to its own 200-day average.
